payload.name: Decompose composite questions into sub-searches
payload.description: When a question asks for an activity or item that must satisfy two independent conditions about the same person—such as something they would enjoy doing AND that benefits their pet—decompose retrieval into separate sub-searches before combining evidence.
content: Before searching, split the question into its independent conditions (for example, 'activity Andrew enjoys' and 'activity involving his dog'). Do not rely on a single composite query.

Run at least one targeted search for each condition separately (e.g., hobbies/preferences/interests; pet-related memories), then intersect the returned memory sets to identify candidates satisfying both conditions.
Stop once each condition has at least one supporting memory; do not add further expansion searches.

solves: Single composite queries for multi-condition questions (e.g., an activity a person enjoys that also involves their pet) over-weight one condition and miss memories supporting each condition separately. Applies when a question requires combining a person's enjoyment/hobby with a pet-related benefit. Does not apply when one memory already directly answers the question.
